pr_title: Make left panel height flexible to avoid overflow
pr_body:
Fixes #1127 

### Changes
- Modify markup to move the zoom button to left menus
- Add some styles for left center menu
- Remove unused menu related classes

![panel_overflow_final](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4126644/78262270-4935bc00-753b-11ea-9062-c931eab5fe66.gif)

check https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/commit/c41f3983fbb7d3f10a83e4a816eca76b22f05b33

Much nicer experience..
@dwelle As you say, I think your solution would be better if only the issue of box-shadow disappearing and panel positioning centered is resolved. I don't know the CSS grid yet. But I'll try more :)

The box-shadow can be fixed by moving it from that particular `.Island` to `.App-right-menu`.

As for positioning, I have no idea either. I'm new to grid as well.
I re-implemented by changing CSS and markup.
There's still a problem with the menu area. I'll check more.
It's nicer indeed.. but why it has a full height?!
@lipis That's the problem! I haven't found a way to make it scrollable without taking up the whole area. I'll dig it more.
Kind looks nice.. but it's a lot of empty space that could be used for scene area :) Thanks
On the other hand, I kind like it the way it is! It's a dead space anyway.. usually people don't draw there.

I agree. Even if you enter the dead zone, you can move out of it, so I think it is better than the situation where you [cannot use some tools](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/810438/77864469-960a5180-7220-11ea-853e-6410efeaa4d2.png).
Of course it's best to get rid of that area, but it's still hard to find a way. 😢
What if we just made the whole side thing scroll? (i.e. the vertical stack)

> What if we just made the whole side thing scroll? (i.e. the vertical stack)

Like this? It is possible with 4 lines of css!

That’s the idea, although it would be nice to still be able to use the zoom buttons.

> That’s the idea, although it would be nice to still be able to use the zoom buttons.

I solved that by hardcoding `height: calc(100vh - 60px)` instead of `height: 100vh`.
@dwelle Yes, I'm working the same way, I'll commit it soon.
![panel_overflow_final](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4126644/78373256-528b5b00-7605-11ea-882f-7e7acbd1c3c1.gif)
